The paper presents a unified approximation for scattering from thin dielectric disks.
The approximation models the internal fields as those of a dielectric slab.
The solution is valid for all frequencies when A/T >> 1.
When T << λ, the solution reduces to an electrostatic (Rayleigh) approximation.
When A >> λ, the solution becomes a physical optics approximation.
The theory was validated against experimental radar cross section measurements.
Measurements were performed for disks with A/T = 3000 and kA = 225.
Measurements were also performed for disks with A/T ≈ 5 and kA ≈ 0.75.
The agreement between theory and experiment is best near nadir (0° incidence).
Edge effects become significant at large incidence angles and for thicker disks.
The theory neglects edge effects, which is its main limitation.
The solution reduces to the Born approximation for small dielectric contrast.
The Fresnel reflection coefficient is used in the radar cross section formula.
The dyadic Green's function relates internal fields to scattered fields.
The incident wave is resolved into horizontal and vertical polarization components.
The Fourier transform of the disk's shape is used in the solution.
The theory accounts for lossy dielectric materials.
The typical A/T ratio for soybean leaves is about 500.
The theory is suitable for modeling natural objects like leaves and ice crystals.
The solution is expressed in closed form and applies for all frequencies.
The approximation is based on a canonical solution to Maxwell's equations.
The theory is most accurate when edge effects are negligible.
The main conclusion is that the theory provides a good approximation for thin disks across all frequencies.
The theory is validated for both high and low frequency regimes.
The solution is derived for arbitrary disk orientation and shape.
